codingChallenge.solutionExample:
## Final Capstone Verification

### 1. Auth hardening checklist (confirm each):
- [x] Passwords hashed with bcrypt, never stored in plaintext - confirmed directly in the database
- [x] JWTs expire correctly - confirmed via a deliberately expired token returning 401
- [x] Every protected route requires valid authentication - confirmed via direct API testing without a token
- [x] Every user-specific resource checks ownership - confirmed by attempting to access another test user's resource by guessing its ID, correctly receiving a 403

### 2. Single critical E2E flow:
Signup -> add a client -> add a project for that client -> see it on
the dashboard. Confirmed passing against my live, deployed URL
(not localhost), including the correct due-date sorting on the dashboard.

### 3. Live deployment direct verification:
Visited my live URL as a stranger. Signed up with a new test account,
added a client and project, confirmed the dashboard correctly showed
it. Tried an invalid email format on signup - correctly rejected with
a clear error. Tried a negative due-date-adjacent value - correctly
rejected by backend validation.

## Findings and fixes:
1. Found that one endpoint (PATCH /projects/:id) was missing its
   resource-ownership check - fixed and re-verified directly.
2. Confirmed no further issues after re-testing the complete flow
   against the live URL following the fix above.
validationRules: Must confirm or explicitly address each item on the auth-hardening checklist with direct evidence, not just an unchecked assumption
The named E2E flow must be the single most critical flow for the student's own brief, and must be confirmed against the LIVE deployed URL, not just localhost
Must include genuine, direct findings from visiting the live application as a skeptical stranger, including at least one adversarial input attempt
Any genuine finding must include a concrete fix and re-verification, not just an acknowledgment
hints: Test ownership checks by deliberately attempting to access a DIFFERENT test user's resource by guessing or modifying an ID - a passing check should reject this with 403
Testing against the live URL specifically (not localhost) is what actually confirms your real production configuration and deployment, exactly this stage's central distinction
If you genuinely find zero issues during this final check, that's a valid outcome - but make sure your adversarial testing was genuinely thorough, not superficial

finalModuleProject.title: Your Deployed, Production-Grade Full Stack SaaS Application
finalModuleProject.goal: Like Module 11's Level 1 capstone, this capstone's 'final project' is not a separate, additional deliverable — it is the single, complete, deployed SaaS application you have already built progressively across this module's 6 stages. This entry exists to formally define the certification bar for Level 2 as a whole, consolidating Stage 6's final checklist into the official completion requirements.
finalModuleProject.description: Your finished capstone must be a single, live, deployed full stack SaaS application meeting every requirement established across Stages 1 through 6: a deliberately scoped project brief with explicit non-goals (Stage 1), a complete, evidence-justified system design document (Stage 2), a fully typed, faithfully-implemented frontend matching that design (Stage 3), an independently-correct, layered backend with its own complete server-side validation (Stage 4), a verified, evidence-backed database layer with justified indexes and (where applicable) genuinely tested transactions (Stage 5), and hardened authentication, a complete testing pyramid including one genuinely critical E2E test, and a real, live, working deployment (Stage 6). There is no separate project to start from scratch here — successfully completing Stages 1 through 6 in sequence IS the completion of this project.

requirements.requirement: A written project brief with a specific core user, core problem, 3-5 core features, and an explicit non-goals list (Stage 1)
A complete system design document addressing all 8 architectural dimensions, each with a specific justification tied to the actual brief (Stage 2)
A fully typed, faithfully-implemented frontend matching the design document, with client-side validation explicitly understood as UX-only (Stage 3)
An independently-correct, layered backend (Repository/Service/Controller) with complete, independent server-side validation and resource-ownership checks (Stage 4)
A verified database layer with schema matching the design document, EXPLAIN-justified indexes, and (if applicable) a genuinely tested transaction rollback (Stage 5)
Hardened authentication, a complete test pyramid including one genuinely critical E2E test against the live URL, and a real, live, working deployment, directly verified by visiting it (Stage 6)

rubric.criterion: The project brief is specifically scoped, with genuine non-goals protecting against scope creep
The system design document provides specific, evidence-based justification for every architectural decision
The frontend faithfully implements the design document with full TypeScript typing and correct state-management tool usage
The backend is independently correct, with complete server-side validation and consistent resource-ownership enforcement
The database layer is verified with genuine EXPLAIN evidence and, where applicable, tested transaction rollback correctness
Authentication is hardened, the test pyramid is complete with a meaningful E2E test, and the application is genuinely, verifiably live and deployed

finalModuleProject.certificateUnlockCondition: Score 70 or above on the rubric across all 6 stages, with a genuinely live, reachable deployed URL and all 6 stage coding challenges completed. Successful completion of this capstone marks the completion of Level 2 and unlocks Level 3.
